Abstract:

Next-generation sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks are expected to provide ubiquitous connectivity, high reliability, enhanced security, and seamless communication across terrestrial, aerial, maritime, and remote regions. To meet these requirements, communication architectures need to support wide-area coverage, flexible relaying, and robust operation under practical channel impairments. In this context, space-air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs) have emerged as a promising framework by integrating satellites, high-altitude platform stations (HAPSs), unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and terrestrial communication networks. However, practical SAGIN deployment is affected by severe path loss, atmospheric turbulence, shadowing, blockage, co-channel interference (CCI), and eavesdropping. A UAV-assisted uplink SAGIN employing hybrid radio-frequency/free-space optical (RF/FSO) transmission in the presence of multiple co-channel interferers is considered. Nakagami-m, Shadowed-Rician, and Gamma-Gamma channel models are employed to characterize the terrestrial RF, satellite RF, and FSO links, respectively. The reliability of the considered architecture is characterized in terms of outage probability under different interference and fading conditions. Physical-layer security is further investigated for an RF-based UAV-assisted SAGIN in the presence of CCI and a malicious UAV eavesdropper. The eavesdropper intercepts the transmissions from both the terrestrial source and UAV relay and applies maximal-ratio combining (MRC) to the received signals. The secrecy performance is characterized in terms of secrecy outage probability under different fading conditions, target secrecy rates, eavesdropper SNRs, interference levels, and satellite shadowing conditions. A downlink HAPS-assisted SAGIN employing a UAV-mounted reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is also considered to support communication when the direct HAPS-to-ground link is unavailable due to blockage. The terrestrial destination is affected by multiple independent and non-identically distributed (i.n.i.d.) co-channel interferers. The performance of the RIS-assisted architecture is characterized through outage probability, ergodic capacity, high-SNR asymptotic analysis, and diversity order. The analytical and asymptotic expressions are validated through Monte Carlo simulations. Overall, the considered frameworks address reliability, physical-layer security, interference, blockage, and intelligent propagation control in SAGIN-enabled future 6G communication networks.
